text:
maria: FYI seeing a spike in 99th/99.9th write latency on ephemeral NVMe in eu-west-1 starting ~02:10 UTC. GPUs get provisioned but pod scheduling waits on local disk readiness, delaying batch jobs by ~30–90s.
jamal: Can you paste the iostat/smart output? Which instances? any common firmware?
maria: gnode-784/gnode-792/gnode-799. Quick iostat snapshot:
```
Device: rrqm/s wrqm/s r/s w/s rkB/s wkB/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await r_await w_await svctm %util
nvme0n1    0.00  6.00  1.00 85.00  16.00 3456.00  82.00    0.62  10.40  0.10 10.40  0.30  3.00
nvme1n1    0.00  1.00  0.00 12.00   0.00  512.00  85.33    0.75  57.50  0.00 57.50  0.50  6.00
```
maria: smartctl shows firmware v3.2.1 on nvme1 across impacted nodes and increasing media errors/wear alerts on the same PCI addresses.
priya: Storage-bot alerted earlier about higher write amplification for these batch types. @theo did we recently change scrub frequency or background GC on those hosts?
theo: We bumped ephemeral cleaner concurrency last week to improve reclaim time for heavy job churn. That increases write churn temporarily. Might be exposing drives with marginal write latency tail.
jamal: Ok that explains workload change. For immediate mitigation I can flip the cleaner throttle and set a backoff window for eu-west-1. Suggest min-concurrency=2, max=6 until we stabilize.
maria: That would help. Also want to avoid mass eviction flaps — scheduler is currently holding GPUs while kubelet waits for local-volume mounts. Can we relax mount readiness check for ephemeral volumes for non-prod pools?
theo: We can add a temporary feature flag: kubelet-local-check=skip-mount-liveness for pool=batch-eu-test. But risks of starting jobs with degraded IO. Prefer to route new batch jobs to other zones for 1–2 hours while we triage.
priya: I can flip routing policy to avoid eu-west-1 for low-latency GPU jobs. But cost/packaging impact: those jobs will go to on-demand in us-west and increase cost. Would like an estimate of expected extra cost if we shift ~20% of batch traffic for 3 hours.
jamal: Quick heuristic: 20% shift to on-demand => ~+12% GPU spend for that window. We have buffer in committed capacity; ops finance ok to cover short-term.
maria: Short-term plan:
- jamal: throttle cleaner concurrency in eu-west-1 (now)
- priya: route low-latency batch jobs away (in 10m)
- theo: start drive healthscan and collect nvme logs (nvme-cli smart-log) from listed nodes (now)
- if errors > threshold mark device MIGHT_BE_BAD and cordon node-local-disk (not whole node)
storage-bot: Automated note: run `nvme smart-log /dev/nvme1n1` and `dmesg | grep -i nvme` — failing writes >5 in 5m triggers alert.
maria: jamal, can you push a quick hotfix to cleaner: set concurrency=2 and sleep-ms=200 between batches? Keep patch small.
jamal: pushed: rollout id 20260318-cleaner-hotfix -> applied to eu-west-1 canary (50% nodes) now. Observability: added metric cleaner.write_ops_rate.
oncall-bot: @maria assigned incident-1667 (nvme-write-tail-eu-west) to eng-infra oncall.
priya: routing changes applied. Low-latency tests show <10s scheduler delay post-shift.
maria: healthscan results so far: two nodes show repeated transport error codes and nvme1 SMART Media_Wear_Limit > 78%. Extracts:
```
Node gnode-792 nvme1 smart: Media_Wear_Limit = 79
Node gnode-799 nvme1 smart: Media_Wear_Limit = 80
```
maria: Not deadly yet but correlated with tail spikes. Next steps we discussed:
- schedule firmware rollback/upgrade for nvme1 v3.2.1 across impacted hosts after maintenance window
- add a temporary rate-limit for ephemeral cleaner writes and increase scrub backoff
- long term: add probe to node health that tracks 95/99 write latency per-device and auto-schedule local-disk-retire when sustained
theo: I'll open a PR for auto-retire heuristics and a playbook for node-local-disk cordon-only (so GPU scheduling can continue on unaffected devices).
jamal: After rolling cleaner throttle, write latency at 99.9 dropped ~40% on canary nodes. Still watching.
maria: Good. Keep monitoring for 2h and if errors persist begin rolling replacement for devices with Media_Wear_Limit >= 85.
priya: Noted. I'll update cost-owner and runbook with the temporary routing and expected spend delta.
maria: Thanks team. cc @storage-bot will keep posting SMART updates every 5m.
